# Review

## Summary

The note is a standing query: how should a KB note be judged worth keeping or selecting as autonomous production grows, beyond repo and collection goals? Its commitments are a stakes section, a current answer made of five partial lenses, and a list of unsettled problems. No branch competes with that question.

## Main claim and side material

- **Stakes.** The maintenance-capacity link and the retirement condition both say why the question matters and when it closes. They are scope, not branches.
- **Current answer.** Each lens is one or two sentences that point to a theory note. The sentence on a claim's test record versus its theory fit is the closest thing to a side distinction. It still sharpens the "validity separate from value" lens, because it separates being well-tested from being useful to the current theory. It is short enough not to weaken the note.
- **Unsettled.** The root-questions item is the longest, and it brings in query-centered root notes and closed citation loops. It stays on topic because it says exactly where the link-based proxy from the current answer fails as a valuation signal. The other three items (asymmetric selection pressure, cold-start admission, combining signals without Goodharting) each name an open problem in valuation itself. The asymmetric-pressure item partly repeats the urgency from Stakes, but it adds the conjecture about which qualities are underselected, so it is not redundant.

None of the side material needs to be removed, demoted, or moved to its own note.

# Review

## Summary

The note is a standing query, so its core commitment is a two-part answer: Commonplace values notes through five partial lenses rather than one rule, and no tested selection mechanism yet decides between valid and valuable notes under autonomous production. In one sentence: *Commonplace judges note value through five partial lenses (answerability, validity-versus-value, reader update, counterfactual use and structural proxies) without a tested way to combine them, which matters because autonomous production can accumulate valid but low-value notes faster than curation removes them.*

The structure makes that sentence easy to recover. The title states the question. The Stakes section names the risk of well-formed clutter and the retirement condition. The Current answer opens with a plain thesis line ("spreads note valuation across five partial lenses rather than one rule"), and bolded lens labels keep each bullet subordinate to it. The Unsettled bullets follow from that answer: cold start, combining signals and asymmetric selection pressure. They do not compete with it.

The one drag is the first Stakes paragraph. Its first sentence gives examples of collection quality bars and an inline gloss before the paragraph says what those goals fail to cover. This makes the opening slightly less memorable but does not hide the claim, so the outcome is PASS with an INFO finding.

A possible revision target is the asymmetric-selection-pressure point in Unsettled: validity is checked more strongly than value. It is arguably the sharpest mechanism behind the note's urgency. Stakes already gestures at it ("high-value notes from merely valid ones"), so naming it there would tie the stakes to the Unsettled bullet. That change is optional and does not affect this check's outcome.

# How do we value notes?

## Stakes

Root `AGENTS.md` and each collection's `COLLECTION.md` set baseline scope and quality bars, such as [explanatory-reach](../theory/first-principles-reasoning-selects-for-explanatory-reach-over.md) (how broadly an explanation transfers beyond the cases that produced it) in `kb/theory/` or fidelity and economy in `kb/reference/`. Those goals decide what a collection admits in principle, but they do not exhaust how to rank, keep, or reject candidate notes.

The question becomes urgent as autonomous production increases note volume. Every retained artifact adds maintenance, navigation, and exposure cost; [maintenance capacity must match harmful-artifact inflow](../theory/maintenance-capacity-must-match-harmful-artifact-inflow.md). Without a clearer way to distinguish high-value notes from merely valid ones, autonomous authoring can accumulate well-formed clutter faster than review and curation can keep up.

This query stays open as long as candidate selection relies on ad-hoc judgment rather than a tested valuation practice; it would narrow or retire once Commonplace adopts and validates an explicit selection mechanism.

## Current answer

Commonplace currently spreads note valuation across five partial lenses rather than one rule:

- **Admission and answerability.** A note enters a knowledge collection only when it is [answerable](../reference/definitions/answerability.md): its contract can name what referent or outcome it answers to, what correctness or currency property it asserts, and what discrepancy triggers revision or retirement.
- **Validity separate from value.** [Choosing what to learn requires both validity and learning-value gates](../theory/choosing-what-to-learn-requires-both-validity-and-learning-value-gates.md): a note can be grounded and coherent yet redundant or too narrow to justify its maintenance cost. Similarly, [a claim's test record does not determine its fit in a working theory](../theory/a-claims-test-record-does-not-determine-its-fit-in-a-working-theory.md) separates whether a claim is well-tested from whether it helps the current theory handle its problem.
- **Reader update and comparative work gain.** For substantive writing, [warranted reader update is the objective of substantive writing](../theory/warranted-reader-update-is-the-objective-of-substantive-writing.md) asks what nontrivial change the note warrants relative to the intended reader and existing KB beyond a generic treatment. [Defining improvement for open-ended work](../theory/defining-improvement-for-open-ended-work.md) grounds that test in expected downstream work and compares adding a note against a cheaper alternative such as adding a link to an existing record.
- **Counterfactual use in live work.** Where no fixed oracle decides theory fit, [system use is an initial selection environment when theory fit lacks a fixed oracle](../theory/system-use-selects-theory-fit-without-a-fixed-oracle.md) looks for counterfactual effect: whether withholding or replacing a note actually changes search, diagnosis, decisions, or recovery.
- **Structural and curation proxies.** For ranking at scale, [notes need quality scores to scale curation](../theory/notes-need-quality-scores-to-scale-curation.md) and [quality signals for KB evaluation](../theory/quality-signals-for-kb-evaluation.md) combine structural maturity (type), review verdicts, recency, and link-strength-weighted inbound links.

## Unsettled

- **Root questions versus sub-questions inside notes.** Weighted inbound links measure reuse when one note answers a local sub-question raised inside another note — what Commonplace's reader-need labels (`grounds`, `mechanism`, `defined-in`, `evidenced-by` in [link vocabulary](../reference/link-vocabulary.md)) already express. Thinking also organizes directly around recurring **root questions** rather than a single claim. Without explicit query-centered notes as roots, a top-level note that answers a live question can look orphaned if no other claim cites it, while a tightly linked cluster can answer each other's sub-questions in a closed loop without serving any real inquiry. We have no established way to represent query-centered root notes or propagate value from them down through answering notes and their subroutines.
- **Asymmetric selection pressure under autonomous production.** Structural validation, source grounding, and critique gates check validity more strongly than anything checks learning value or reader update. Under the conjecture that [weakly discriminated qualities tend to be underselected](../theory/weakly-discriminated-qualities-tend-to-be-underselected.md), an autonomous authoring loop can enrich accepted notes more strongly for validity than for usefulness, and if production favors fluent local additions, clutter can accumulate.
- **Cold-start selection at admission.** Inbound links and counterfactual system use only become observable after a note has been retained and used. Autonomous production needs a way to filter, quarantine, or trial new candidates before those downstream signals exist.
- **Combining dimensions without Goodharting.** Even where several signals exist (reader update, subroutine reuse, demand-root coverage, counterfactual use, maintenance cost), we do not yet know how to weigh them or when a coarse triage check outperforms a composite score.

---

Relevant Notes:

- [Choosing what to learn requires both validity and learning-value gates](../theory/choosing-what-to-learn-requires-both-validity-and-learning-value-gates.md) — see-also: separates trustworthiness from whether a candidate earns its maintenance burden
- [Warranted reader update is the objective of substantive writing](../theory/warranted-reader-update-is-the-objective-of-substantive-writing.md) — see-also: defines substantive writing value relative to the reader's prior and existing KB
- [Notes need quality scores to scale curation](../theory/notes-need-quality-scores-to-scale-curation.md) — see-also: candidate structural and review signals for ranking notes as the corpus grows
- [System use is an initial selection environment when theory fit lacks a fixed oracle](../theory/system-use-selects-theory-fit-without-a-fixed-oracle.md) — see-also: counterfactual use in live work as a selection signal when no fixed oracle exists
- [Answerability](../reference/definitions/answerability.md) — evidenced-by: Commonplace's admission invariant naming referent, asserted property, and revision trigger

---
description: "Synthesize a compression review into at most three high-level simplifications that materially improve the artifact but still require authorial judgment"
type: types/instruction.md
depth: 4
---

# Synthesize high-impact simplification opportunities

Read the complete artifact and the individual compression findings. Report only opportunities likely to materially improve a reader's understanding of the central claim, conceptual structure, or argumentative flow. Do not edit the artifact.

An opportunity qualifies when its benefit would be large but its implementation requires broader judgment. Typical cases include surfacing a buried thesis, making the role of a load-bearing paragraph explicit, combining several local findings into one deletion or fold, or reorganizing an explanation whose current sequence hides the argument. Exclude local wording improvements, cosmetic changes, minor compression, and alternatives that are merely different.

The synthesis may combine several gate findings or identify a global reorganization visible only after reading the artifact as a whole. Ground every opportunity in the artifact or the gate findings; do not invent a stronger thesis for the artifact to serve.

Distinguish a buried contribution from an undetermined one. A contribution supported by the artifact can be surfaced or given a clearer role. If the artifact does not select among materially different theses, audiences, or purposes, report the missing choice under `Preserve or decide`; do not choose one merely to make the prose cohere. This isolated synthesis receives no retained-intent input, so do not import the choice from the topic, a bare writing prompt, or ambient conversation. The calling workflow may later resolve it from explicit user direction or a separate memory input. A [bare writing prompt does not determine its intended contribution](../../theory/a-bare-writing-prompt-does-not-determine-its-intended-contribution.md).

If the simplification depends on choosing among materially different meanings, conceptual roles, evidence claims, or substantive conclusions, name that unresolved choice as a prerequisite. Do not resolve it as a compression edit. Semantic gates or the author must settle it first.

Return zero to three opportunities. For each one, give:

- the location and smallest useful quotation or section range;
- the important reader problem;
- the direction a revision could take;
- the compression findings it combines, if any; and
- the meanings, implications, or structural choices the author must resolve or preserve.

Do not present a rewrite as settled. A short candidate formulation may illustrate the opportunity, but label it as one possible resolution. Keep fact-checking, claim evaluation, and general completeness review outside this synthesis unless they are necessary to explain why the simplification cannot safely proceed.

## Running it alone

The [compression bundle](../run-compression-bundle-on-note.md) applies this synthesis after its four checks, under the bundle's own output contract. The inputs and output below apply when the synthesis runs alone.

### Inputs

The compression findings are explicit input files, one per check, such as the four check results under `kb/workflow-state/data/current/review/results/<note-path>/`. Run the synthesis alone:

```bash
commonplace-review NOTE --criteria compression-synthesis \
  --input core-claim-obscured=PATH --input branch-bloat=PATH \
  --input detail-overhang=PATH --input marginal-value-redundancy=PATH
```

Use only the supplied findings. Do not run a check, and do not look for other findings. The run keeps its result as a retained observation and writes no current result, because no freshness hash covers the supplied findings.

### Output

The caller names the output file. Write only that file; mutate nothing else. The output is a [review result](../../types/review-result.md) fragment with `outcome: report` and no `attack-outcome`. Each opportunity is one finding, zero to three in all. Give it `scope: passage` with its smallest useful quotation, or `scope: document` with no quotes for a section range or a cross-cutting change. Its `reason` states the reader problem and the direction.

```markdown
---
type: types/review-result.md
findings:
  - scope: passage
    quotes: ["<smallest useful quotation>"]
    reason: "<reader problem>; <direction a revision could take>"
outcome: report
---

# Simplification synthesis: <note title>

## Opportunities

### 1. <short opportunity name>

- Location: <heading and quotation or section range>
- Combines: <the compression findings, or "cross-cutting">
- Preserve or decide: <meanings, implications or structural choices the author must resolve or preserve>
```

Write `None` under `## Opportunities` when no opportunity clears the threshold.

---
type: types/type-spec.md
name: review-result
description: "One completed gate, conformance or report-method assessment with structured findings and controller-owned execution provenance"
schema: ./review-result.schema.yaml
---

# Review result

A review result records one assessment of captured target text against a criterion. Completion means the output passed deterministic checks, not that its judgment is correct. A report outcome is not a favorable verdict. Use this type for individual gate, compression-check, type-conformance and collection-conformance verdicts, and for critique, composition-friction, premise-decomposition and compression-synthesis reports and role reports. Do not use it for combined improvement packets or connection discovery.

## Content

Findings state what the assessed text establishes or fails to establish. Each passage finding quotes enough verbatim text to identify one contiguous span uniquely. A quote is matched after whitespace and typographic quote marks are normalized, so a line wrap in the target does not break it. A quote therefore identifies a passage and is not a byte-exact copy of it. A consumer that needs the exact span locates the quote in the captured target, which holds the exact bytes. A document-wide or absence finding explains the condition without inventing a quotation. Finding levels belong to verdict criteria; critique reports instead state whether the strongest attack lands and how the note engages it. An empty findings list is an honest completed result when no finding remains.

The body explains the assessment without repeating every structured finding. A critique preserves its central commitment, critique mode, strongest case, the note's response and constructive findings, including why an attack does not survive. Low-confidence no-surviving-attack findings leave the need for a domain check visible.

Each report method has its own shape, which the schema checks by the result's `criterion`:

| Method | Findings | Required body |
|---|---|---|
| Critique | constructive findings | `attack-outcome` in frontmatter; `## Strongest case against it`, `## How the note engages it`, `## Constructive findings` |
| Composition friction | the surfaced joints, thinnest first; each reason begins `UNSUPPORTED`, `THIN` or `HOLDS` | a `**Filter:** SURVIVES` or `DISSOLVES` line; `## Filter`, `## Thinnest joints`, `## For the human` |
| Premise decomposition | one per premise; each reason begins `HOLDS`, `DOUBTFUL` or `DEFEATED`, and a non-`HOLDS` reason names `LOCAL` or `GLOBAL` and `instance`, `prevalence` or `priced-exception` | a `**Register:**` line; `## Premises and counterexamples`, `## For the human` |
| Compression synthesis | zero to three opportunities | `## Opportunities` |
| Role report | one per dependent need, duplication or untaken recommendation; each reason begins `SUPPLIED`, `PARTLY SUPPLIED`, `NOT SUPPLIED`, `DUPLICATED` or `UNTAKEN` | `## Role`, `## Dependents`, `## Duplication`, `## Untaken recommendations`, `## Reach` |

Only critique supplies `attack-outcome`. Friction's filter line and the premise statuses route attention; they are not overall verdicts. A report criterion is named by its library instruction's identity, so moving one of these instructions requires a schema edit.

## Field ownership

The worker fragment supplies only `type`, `findings`, `outcome`, optional `attack-outcome`, and the body. Findings precede the outcome so the serialized verdict follows its rationale. The fragment is not a complete saved artifact. The controller completes and validates it; workers never assert hashes, execution identities or timestamps.

| Fields | Owner and meaning |
|---|---|
| `type`, `findings`, `outcome`, `attack-outcome` | Worker assessment; findings contain `scope`, `quotes`, `reason`, and `level` for verdicts |
| `description`, `format`, `contract` | Controller's result-format identity and expected verdict/report contract |
| `note`, `criterion` | Original target and criterion identities |
| `note-sha256`, `criterion-sha256` | Freshness hashes; the note hash may cover normalized watched parts, not exact bytes |
| `target-sha256`, `target-capture` | Exact assessed UTF-8 bytes and their retained repository-relative location |
| `observation`, `contract-sha256` | Execution observation and captured output-contract identity |
| `profile`, `model`, `run`, `launch`, `completed-at` | Requested execution configuration and observed execution provenance |
| `raw-output`, `raw-output-sha256` | Retained original worker fragment, distinct from this completed artifact |

## Template

Worker fragment for a verdict criterion; code supplies the remaining fields:

```markdown
---
type: types/review-result.md
findings:
  - scope: document
    quotes: []
    reason: "The claim omits the condition needed for its stated conclusion."
    level: warn
outcome: warn
---

# Review

## Summary

The conclusion needs its missing condition.
```

A critique fragment uses `outcome: report`, supplies `attack-outcome`, and omits finding levels. Its body retains the critique instruction's sections. Other report fragments use `outcome: report`, omit `attack-outcome` and finding levels, and follow their instruction's Output section. Neither fragment uses a terminal `## Result:` line. Operational production and publication belong to the review command, not to this type.

type: types/collection-contract.md
description: "Workflow-owned records used to continue a run, inspect a result, or recover an earlier decision; not the retained reports a clean checkout can cite."

# Workflow state

## Purpose

Use this collection to answer questions such as “Why did this run stop?” or “Which finding did the operator already decide?” A record belongs here when a named workflow owns it and reads it or keeps it to explain its work. Completion does not make the record disposable. Put an exact report readers need in a clean checkout in `kb/reports/retained/`; put an unfinished investigation in `kb/work/`.

## Layout and maintenance

The main repository owns this contract and the landing. New workflow payloads belong under `data/current/`, one directory per producing workflow. Older records beside `current/` are historical evidence, not inputs to current commands. Keep embedded paths in those records unchanged. The whole payload tree can be a separate checkout. A main-repository clone need not contain it.

Keep the identifiers, paths and evidence the owning workflow uses. Follow its filename, title and description conventions; do not rename a generated record for readability. Attribute inputs and judgments as required by the workflow. Staged candidates retain their destination format; keep exact captures unchanged. The state repository's README identifies what deletion loses for each workflow. Only the owning workflow sets the cleanup rule.

## Outbound links

A record may point inline to any KB collection to identify its inputs, outputs or governing procedure, or to an external source when the workflow records it as evidence. Keep references used by the workflow resolvable. Do not add formal footer links or topic tags to run records for discovery. Tags and links in an exact capture describe the captured artifact, not this collection.
